I have the Oracle upper on my home build. Why not just mill your own receiver? You can to it for a whole lot cheaper and it leaves you with a little extra in your budget for glass. Even building it off a complete receiver would be cheaper and just as good.

I watched a video of a not-mechanically-inclined guy try to mill his own lower, just to see how easy it was, and he fucked it up really bad. That would probably be how my experience would turn out.

And, yeah, looking at the Oracle, I'll most likely end up trading out most of the stock parts anyway.

How do you build off a complete lower? I mean, it just comes as a hollowed out piece of metal and you put the trigger assembly in?

My wife milled her own lower and it turned out great. If you have the right tools and you take your time you will succeed and end up with a high quality functional lower. To build off a complete lower is as simple as installing the trigger assembly and safety selector. You can buy complete trigger assemblies which will make the process easier and give you a better quality trigger. I've done both and found installing a competition trigger to be a lot easier. Also building off a complete 308 lower is a lot easier than an AR-15 lower in my opinion because you don't have to deal with any roll pins. There are videos on YouTube (or there used to be, I hope they're still there) on how to install the lower parts and it's not as hard as it looks.
Milling 80% lowers is easy. It was probably a clickbait video. That said, don't do it to save money, because you won't.
